summary: A Best Current Practice on how IETF protocols use Ethernet frame formats and IEEE 802 parameters. It sets the IANA rules for allocating code points under the IANA Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI), and updates RFC 2153. It was replaced by RFC 7042.

eli5.summary: Network gear uses numbers assigned by the IEEE, like a company prefix on a barcode. This sets the rules for how the IETF hands out its own numbers from that range. It has been replaced by RFC 7042.

questions: who approves iana ethernet address allocations
subtitle: How IANA hands out Ethernet addresses and protocol numbers from the IETF's own block of IEEE space.

tldr.problem: Some IETF protocols need Ethernet MAC identifiers and IEEE 802 protocol identifiers, and IANA needed clear rules for allocating them under its own Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI).
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes the IANA OUI 00-00-5E, what has been allocated under it, and who must approve each size of allocation: Expert Review for small and medium requests, IESG Ratification for large ones and for reserved values.
tldr.outcome: It also deprecates the 'CF Series' of OUIs from RFC 2153. The document was later obsoleted by RFC 7042.

today: RFC 5342 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 141) that has been obsoleted by RFC 7042, so RFC 7042 is the current version of these rules. It updated RFC 2153.

sections.title: Scope and the IANA OUI
sections.content:
Some IETF protocols use Ethernet or other IEEE 802 frame formats and parameters, including MAC (Media Access Control) identifiers and protocol identifiers. This document specifies IANA considerations for allocating code points under the IANA OUI, and discusses other IETF use of IEEE 802 code points.

The registration authority for Ethernet parameters, originally Xerox Corporation, is now the IEEE Registration Authority. Anyone may apply to it, and it may impose fees, though it commonly waives them for standards bodies. The OUI 00-00-5E has been allocated to IANA.

The RFC fixes some notation. Octets are written as two hex digits separated by hyphens, and IAB means Individual Address Block, not the Internet Architecture Board. Security gets a single sentence: the document is not directly concerned with security.
sections.eli5: A big club hands out company codes. The IETF got one code of its own, and this paper sets the rules for giving out numbers under it.

sections.title: EUI-48 and EUI-64 Identifiers
sections.content:
A globally unique 48-bit MAC address (EUI-48) is a 3-octet OUI plus 3 octets assigned by the holder. Two bits in the first octets matter: the Group bit (01-00-00) and the Local bit (02-00-00). Turning on the Group bit makes a multicast identifier; an identifier with the Local bit on is a local one, and the OUI holder has no special authority over it.

The IANA OUI covers 224 multicast identifiers from 01-00-5E-00-00-00 to 01-00-5E-FF-FF-FF and 224 unicast identifiers from 00-00-5E-00-00-00 to 00-00-5E-FF-FF-FF. Allocations so far include 223 multicast identifiers for IPv4 multicast (RFC 1112), 220 for MPLS multicast (RFC 5332) and 28 unicast identifiers for VRRP (RFC 3768).

For 64-bit identifiers, IPv6 forms the lower 64 bits of some addresses from a Modified EUI-64, which inverts the Local/Global bit, for example 02-00-5E-aa-bb-cc-dd-ee. Inserting FF-FE in the middle of an EUI-48 gives the matching Modified EUI-64. The range 02-00-5E-FE-xx-xx-xx-xx is reserved for holders of IPv4 addresses, where xx-xx-xx-xx is the address. The IETF also uses all multicast MAC identifiers beginning 33-33 for IPv6 multicast (RFC 2464).
sections.eli5: A network card's number has two halves: who made it, and which one it is. Two special switches in the number say 'this goes to a whole group' or 'this one was made up locally'.

sections.title: Ethernet Protocol Identifiers
sections.content:
Ethernet protocol parameters say what a frame carries, such as IPv4 or IPv6. Two kinds follow the destination and source addresses. Ethertypes are 16-bit identifiers with a value of at least 0x0600. LSAPs are 8-bit identifiers that appear in pairs after a 16-bit length, which must be below 0x5DC so it cannot be mistaken for an Ethertype. Neither is allocated by IANA; the IEEE Registration Authority does that.

Both can be extended to a five-octet identifier under an OUI. In the IEEE 802 LLC (SNAP) format this looks like xx-xx-AA-AA-03-yy-yy-yy-zz-zz, where yy-yy-yy is the OUI and zz-zz is a number the OUI owner allocates. With an Ethertype, the special OUI Extended Ethertype 88-B7 starts a body with 88-B7-yy-yy-yy-zz-zz.

Under the IANA OUI, 216 protocol numbers from 00-00-5E-00-00 to 00-00-5E-FF-FF exist, with the two extreme values reserved. New allocations must be for standards use, documented in an Internet-Draft or RFC, and not for any protocol that already has an Ethertype. Other OUI-based parameters, such as one-octet specifiers, are also allocated by Expert Review.
sections.eli5: A frame needs a label saying what is inside, like a sticker on a lunchbox. Some stickers are short, and some are long and start with a company code.

sections.title: Allocation Rules and Approval
sections.content:
Every allocation must be for standards purposes, be a power-of-two block starting on a boundary of equal or greater power of two, must not be used to evade the need for vendors to get their own IEEE blocks, and must be documented in an Internet-Draft or RFC.

Approval depends on size. For EUI-48, blocks from 1 up to 65536 (216) need Expert Review, and 131072 (217) or more need IESG Ratification. For EUI-64, Expert Review covers up to 268435456 (228), while any size, including 536870912 (229) or more, may be allocated with IESG Ratification. Reserved values always need IESG Ratification.

The process is: the applicant sends a template to IANA, IANA forwards it to an appointed Expert, and for Expert Review a disapproval denies the request while an approval lets IANA allocate. For ratification the Expert passes a favorable or uncertain opinion to the IESG, which decides. When 90% or more of the multicast or unicast EUI-48 space under 00-00-5E is used, IANA should ask the IEEE for another OUI.
sections.eli5: Small requests need one helper to say yes. Very large ones, or ones from the reserved shelf, also need the big committee to agree.

sections.title: Changes to RFC 2153
sections.content:
RFC 2153 declared the 3-octet values from CF-00-00 through CF-FF-FF to be OUIs that IANA could allocate to software vendors, for example for PPP. When used as MAC prefixes these values have the Local and Group bits on, whereas IEEE-allocated OUIs have them off.

This RFC updates the IANA Considerations of RFC 2153 with no technical changes. Use of these identifiers based on IANA allocation is deprecated, and IANA is directed not to allocate any further values in the 'CF Series'. The text notes that only a handful were allocated in over a decade of availability.
sections.eli5: An old club-number shelf is closed. No new numbers will be handed out from it.

data.code:
SNAP:           xx-xx-AA-AA-03-yy-yy-yy-zz-zz
Ethertype form: 88-B7-yy-yy-yy-zz-zz

xx-xx    frame length
AA       SNAP SAP
03       LLC control octet
yy-yy-yy OUI
zz-zz    protocol number under that OUI
